iss-cabin.implication: Fabric burns readily in cabin-like air in microgravity.
iss-cabin.evidence: Saffire IV burned a 50 cm fabric sample for 130 s at 22.0 % O2, 100 kPa and 20 cm/s concurrent flow, with an average heat release of 3,150 W.

iss-cabin.implication: Lowering airflow can put out a thin-fuel flame near these conditions. This suggests ventilation control matters, but one record is weak evidence.
iss-cabin.evidence: A thin fabric flame ignited at 5 cm/s went out when the flow was reduced to 2.2 cm/s at 18.7 % O2 and 1 atm.

iss-cabin.implication: A material can burn in microgravity below the oxygen level that limits it on Earth.
iss-cabin.evidence: Flame spread over a 9.5 mm PMMA rod at 17.8 % O2 and 100 kPa, below the roughly 18 % normal-gravity flammability limit.

iss-cabin.implication: Most of the remaining close evidence was collected in oxygen-enriched, lower-pressure atmospheres, not in cabin air.
iss-cabin.evidence: Four Saffire burns at 26.2 to 31.0 % O2 and 54.1 to 70.7 kPa all spread.

exploration-atmosphere.implication: No flight test in this dataset matches 34 % O2 at 56.5 kPa. In the closest tests, every sample burned and the flame spread.
exploration-atmosphere.evidence: Saffire VI burned fabric and PMMA at 28.8 to 31.0 % O2 and 54.1 to 55.2 kPa with 20 cm/s concurrent flow.

exploration-atmosphere.implication: Combustion gases reached crew limits in a small spacecraft. This suggests toxic gas is a hazard well away from the flame.
exploration-atmosphere.evidence: PMMA fires pushed cabin CO above the 24-hour crew limit and CO2 above the 1-hour limit in a 16.7 m³ spacecraft.

exploration-atmosphere.implication: Smoke detection can come late, after most of the hazardous gas is already released. One record is weak evidence.
exploration-atmosphere.evidence: Smoke was readily detected only at 981 s, and temperature rose significantly only very near the fire.

exploration-atmosphere.implication: Thick plastic can keep burning for many minutes under these conditions.
exploration-atmosphere.evidence: A 1 cm PMMA slab burned for 780 s and a 0.5 cm one-sided slab for 1,200 s.
